item.content:encoded: How do you propose they contain him? Like the guy said on the first page, if he wanted to escape, all he has to do is cut out his tracker and move as fast as possible away from the Site the next time he shifts. But he hasn't done that during any of his shifts. In fact he makes an effort to get back into containment every time he does wind up off-site. item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I can see why he would have been classified Safe at the time, since the Locked Box analogy wasn't as prevalent then. It's just a regular guy who gets randomly shifted between realities; it was assumed that the worst that could happen with him is that he disappears and randomly appears in public with anomalous stuff. Though, it's possible he could bring back something extremely dangerous to our reality, which is why I would agree with a Keter classification.

Still, I see no reason why he would want to run away. He gets protection, basic living needs, rehabilitation from his trips, and interaction with the paranormal, which he supposedly enjoys (which doesn't make much sense considering his anomalous properties, now that I think about). It'd have to be something like Serpent's Hand to encourage him to escape, with the promise of more freedom and equipment for his trips.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Alright, I like this one. It's an interesting concept and it's well done and well written. I also like the fact that the guy comes across as an average Joe and is rather relatable even though we only get indirect descriptions of his personality and behaviour. Oh and the interview log is fantastic and really adds a new dimension (no pun intended) to this SCP. Seriously, if you've read the main article and skipped that, go check it out, it's worth it.

However, I think a few changes would make this one even better:

+ show block
– hide block

- I find it weird that the article keeps referring to 507 as "it". I know the SCP Foundation tends to think of SCPs as objects, even when they're sentient and humanoid, but most articles still tend to have them refer to an SCP as "he" or "she" when a gender is applicable. Either that or their number.

- Even if the guy is obedient, I don't see the foundation allowing him to interact directly with SCP objects no matter how safe they are as he could easily shift while touching one and cause an accidental breach and potentially lose it.

At the very least I feel that he shouldn't be allowed to interact with other SCPs if it has been at least two weeks since his last shift (but even then it seems irresponsible of the Foundation to just assume that because they never noted less than two weeks between shifts means it can't ever happen).

- Couldn't his ability to take people and objects with him be used to send bodyguards or even researchers with him, with instructions to stay in physical contact with him? At least D-Class people? Similarly, wouldn't it be wise to provide him with a camera so he could more easily document the dimensions he visits?

- I don't think it's got the right object class. It doesn't pass the locked box test, he could be killed in an alternate dimension and stay there, accidentally reveal secrets, bring back something dangerous from an alternate dimension, catch an unknown disease and start an epidemic, accidentally cause a containment breach. In fact, according o the shifts log, many of these things HAVE already happened. And then there's the implications brought up by the interview. The shifts log also implies that they can't even be sure he'll reappear in his quarters. Euclid seems more appropriate to me.

Other random observations:

subject was surprised by a man wearing a black business suit and sunglasses, with an impossibly wide smile.

So… was that 106 in his pocket dimension?

Addendum 507-01: I don’t care how much he grumbles about it; SCP-507 is not to be cleared for challenging SCP-076-2 to fifty rounds of Tic-Tac-Toe. Just…no. -Dr.███

Stuff like this is why I will always defend lolfoundation.
